descriptionChirho: Interrogative temporal adverb meaning 'when?' used in direct and indirect questions about the timing of events. Frequently in the Synoptic apocalyptic discourse: Matt 24:3, 25:37-44; Mark 9:19, 13:4, 13:33, 13:35; Luke 9:41, 12:36, 17:20. Also Matt 17:17. All multilingual glosses consistently render as when/wann/quand/cuándo/언제/מָתַי/مَتَى.

Component of the conjunction mēpote (μήποτε) or similar constructions meaning 'ever, at any time,' typically in clauses expressing apprehension or negative purpose ('lest at any time,' 'lest ever'). Matt 4:6, 5:25, 7:6, 13:15, 13:29, 15:32, 27:64; Mark 4:12, 14:2; Luke 12:58, 14:8, 14:12, 14:29, 21:34; Acts 5:39, 28:27; 2 Tim 2:25; Heb 2:1, 3:12. Glosses: ever/alguna-vez/혹시/أَبَدًا/פֶּן.

Used in constructions suggesting possibility or uncertainty, meaning 'perhaps, possibly, indeed.' In Luke 3:15 the people were wondering whether John might perhaps be the Christ; in John 7:26 the crowds ask whether the authorities have perhaps recognized Jesus as the Christ; Luke 4:11 in the temptation narrative. Glosses: perhaps/acaso/어쩌면/أوّلاي/אוּלַי.
